HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08389

Full Title: AN ACT PROHIBITING POLITICAL DYNASTIES IN NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICES

Short Title: Anti - Political Dynasty Act

Abstract: Aims to ensure equal access to public office and opportunities for public service. Defines “political dynasty” as the concentration, consolidation and dominance of elective political power by spouses or persons to one another and “political dynasty relationship” as an existing familial relationship with an incumbent elective public official, such as spouse, direct ascendant or descendant, sibling, or any other person related within the second degree of consanguinity or affinity, whether legitimate or illegitimate, full or half-blood. Provides that the prohibition shall apply to any of the following political dynasty relationships: Spouses, or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any national elective position; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously running as member of the House of Representatives within the same legislative district; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same provincial government; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same city or municipal government; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same barangay. Mandates the COMELEC to notify all persons where certificate of candidacy will result in a potential political dynasty relationship within a period of five (5) days from the filing of candidacy and also release such notice to the public in any manner that ensures that the persons concerned are informed. Allows the persons belonging to a potential dynasty relation forty-eight (48) hours from the receipt of such notice, or from the posting thereof, to choose amongst themselves which person shall assume office in the event that any two (2) of them obtain favorable results and to submit their joint written agreement to the COMELEC. If no agreement has been reached, the COMELEC shall proceed with the drawing of lots to decide who amongst them may be favored with luck.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08464

Full Title: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE TRAVEL TAX

Short Title: Travel Tax Abolition Act Of 2026

Abstract: Abolishes the travel tax imposed under PD No. 1183, as amended, and Section 73 of RA No. 9593, otherwise known as the “Tourism Act of 2009” as amended. Prohibits the collection of travel tax by any government or private entity upon the law’s effectivity. Mandates immediate refund of previously paid travel taxes for applicable flights. Mandates the National Government to provide necessary funding to TIEZA for tourism development, the Commission on Higher Education for Higher Education Development Fund, and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts for the National Endowment Fund for Culture and the Arts through the annual General Appropriations Act (GAA). Mandates the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) and the Department of Budget and Management to create rules for refunds and transition to GAA funding within 60 days.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08389

Full Title: AN ACT PROHIBITING POLITICAL DYNASTIES IN NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICES

Short Title: Anti - Political Dynasty Act

Abstract: Aims to ensure equal access to public office and opportunities for public service. Defines “political dynasty” as the concentration, consolidation and dominance of elective political power by spouses or persons to one another and “political dynasty relationship” as an existing familial relationship with an incumbent elective public official, such as spouse, direct ascendant or descendant, sibling, or any other person related within the second degree of consanguinity or affinity, whether legitimate or illegitimate, full or half-blood. Provides that the prohibition shall apply to any of the following political dynasty relationships: Spouses, or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any national elective position; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously running as member of the House of Representatives within the same legislative district; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same provincial government; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same city or municipal government; Spouses or relatives within the second degree simultaneously holding any elective office within the same barangay. Mandates the COMELEC to notify all persons where certificate of candidacy will result in a potential political dynasty relationship within a period of five (5) days from the filing of candidacy and also release such notice to the public in any manner that ensures that the persons concerned are informed. Allows the persons belonging to a potential dynasty relation forty-eight (48) hours from the receipt of such notice, or from the posting thereof, to choose amongst themselves which person shall assume office in the event that any two (2) of them obtain favorable results and to submit their joint written agreement to the COMELEC. If no agreement has been reached, the COMELEC shall proceed with the drawing of lots to decide who amongst them may be favored with luck.
